title: Fuzzy logic based hybrid load balancing for solar-grid supply with tiered load shedding: a simulation study
desc: Hybrid installations that combine a solar inverter and battery with the utility grid are increasingly common in Uganda, yet they are typically managed by threshold-based automatic transfer switches (ATS) that ignore solar availability, grid quality, and load criticality. This paper presents the design, modelling, and simulation-based evaluation of a multi-input fuzzy logic based hybrid load balancing controller. The framework fuses four inputs (solar output, battery state of charge (SOC), grid status, and load demand) through a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system to produce two coordinated outputs: a source-priority signal and a tiered load-shedding signal spanning three load classes (critical, flexible, and non-essential). The study is entirely simulation-based. The system was implemented in Python at one-minute resolution over a synthetic but representative 24-hour scenario featuring two grid outages, a brownout, and cloud-induced solar variability, and was benchmarked against a conventional threshold-based transfer switch, an ATS with critical-load priority, and a crisp rule-based tiered controller; it was further tested on seven stress cases and a 100-run Monte Carlo evaluation. In the headline scenario the fuzzy controller sustained 100% availability of critical load against 91.9% for the baseline, which suffered 67 minutes of complete blackout; raised solar utilisation from 47.1% to 100%; cut grid energy from 13.43 kWh to 7.95 kWh (40.8%); and reduced source-switching events from four to two. These gains came from deliberately curtailing all non-essential load and 4.6% of flexible load, so they are not a pure efficiency gain: total unserved energy rose from 1.84 to 3.18 kWh, although a criticality-weighted reliability index still favoured the fuzzy controller (96.4% versus 92.6%). Broader testing confirmed the solar-utilisation and grid-energy advantages over the threshold baseline, but showed that an ATS with simple critical-load priority protected critical load at least as well under stress, identifying rule-base tuning as the main need. The results support a simulation-based proof of concept. A real-time embedded demonstration, in which the controller and plant model ran on a Raspberry Pi 5 with an external touch display using emulated inputs, reproduced the simulated behaviour; testing with live sensors and relays and field validation remain future work.

title: Development of a transparent reporting tool for AI-based diagnostic prediction models of disease and syndrome in Chinese medicine (TRAPODS-CM): a Delphi study
desc: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) prediction models have gained traction in Chinese medicine (CM) diagnostics. However, existing reporting guidelines, largely based on modern medicine diagnostic frameworks, have limited applicability to CM due to fundamental differences in diagnostic approaches. This highlights the need for a tailored reporting standard. This study develops a transparent reporting guideline for CM diagnostic AI models using the Delphi consensus method. An initial checklist was created by a steering committee and core working group, drawing on a prior systematic review, existing guidelines, and the unique characteristics of CM diagnostics. A multidisciplinary panel of 31 experts evaluated each domain and item on a 1–5 Likert scale across multiple Delphi rounds. In the first round, domain consensus was decent (Kendall’s W = 0.498), but item consensus was low (W = 0.271), prompting substantial revisions, including 5 modifications and 1 addition for domains, and 20 modifications, 13 deletions, and 4 additions for items. In the second round, domain consensus remained strong (W = 0.487), while item consensus improved significantly (W = 0.349), indicating convergence on the checklist. A final consensus meeting led to the refinement and finalization of the Transparent Reporting Tool for AI-Based Diagnostic Prediction Models of Disease and Syndrome in Chinese Medicine (TRAPODS-CM). This guideline aims to provide a reporting framework for CM diagnostic AI prediction models where the unique diagnostic principles of CM are specifically addressed, ultimately fostering more transparent, reliable and reproducible AI-driven clinical applications in this field.

title: Blockchain-enhanced SDN framework with deep unfolding spatial frequency attention network and pine cone optimization for smart city IoT cybersecurity
desc: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart cities has revolutionized services by connecting numerous devices to deliver intelligent applications. However, this interconnected environment also exposes IoT networks to severe cybersecurity risks, including data breaches, intrusions, and advanced persistent threats. Traditional detection mechanisms often struggle with high-dimensional traffic, noisy data, missing values, and evolving attack patterns, which significantly reduce their reliability. Moreover, ensuring secure and tamper-proof storage of detection outcomes in large-scale IoT system s remains a major challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-enhanced IoT cybersecurity framework for smart cities, utilizing a software-defined networking framework with a Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network and Pine Cone Optimization (DUSFAN-PCO). Initially, input data is collected from UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017 datasets. The collected data are pre-processed using Diffusion Models for Missing Value Imputation (DMMVI) to handle noise and missing values. Next, Carpet Weaver Optimization (CWO) is applied to select the most informative attributes. These selected features are then fed into the Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network (DUSFAN), which classifies IoT network traffic into normal and multiple attack categories through real-time anomaly detection. To further enhance detection accuracy, Pine Cone Optimization (PCO) is used to fine-tune DUSFAN’s weight parameters. Finally, the results are securely stored and managed using a Blockchain-Based Secure PBFT Lightweight Consensus (SPBFT-LC), ensuring immutability, transparency, and trust among IoT nodes. The proposed DUSFAN-PCO framework achieves an accuracy of 99.20% on UNSW-NB15 and 99.48% on CIC-IDS2017, with F1-scores of 99.52% and 99.50%, and ROC values of 0.99–1.00 across both datasets. Coupled with high blockchain-based security integrity (> 99%), it ensures robust, real-time, and reliable detection of IoT network intrusions, making it highly suitable for secure and resilient smart city IoT environments.
